Total exposure time and total time at risk

Source: R/time_at_risk.R
time_at_risk.Rd

Computes the two exposure measures used by the BDRIBS models of Duncan (2026) from subject-level data. BDRIBS(1) uses the total exposure time (the sum of the follow-up times), and BDRIBS(2) uses the total time at risk, in which the time after the first occurrence of the event is removed.

Usage

time_at_risk(follow_up, event, event_time)

Arguments

follow_up

Numeric vector of follow-up times (positive).

event

Vector of event indicators (1 if the subject had at least one occurrence of the event, 0 otherwise).

event_time

Numeric vector of times to the first occurrence of the event. Values for subjects without the event are not used and may be NA.

Value

A named numeric vector with elements exposure (total exposure time), time_at_risk (total time at risk), and n_event (number of subjects with the event).

References

Duncan, B. (2026). Robust safety monitoring and signal detection using alternatives to the standard Poisson distribution. Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics, 36(2), 227–244. doi:10.1080/10543406.2024.2395532

See also

bdribs_post

Examples

time_at_risk(follow_up = c(52, 52, 30, 12),
             event = c(1, 0, 1, 0),
             event_time = c(10, NA, 25, NA))
#>     exposure time_at_risk      n_event 
#>          146           99            2
